findings.title: Member list rendering broken due to incorrect each helper syntax
findings.body: The template uses `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` without the opening `#`. In Ember, block helpers require `{{#each ...}}`. As written, this is treated as an inline helper returning nothing, and the members are never iterated. Additionally, there is no closing `{{/each}}`. This causes the admin group members list to be empty. The line should be `{{#each member in members itemView="group-member"}} ... {{/each}}`.

findings.title: Spec uses wrong HTTP verb for remove_member automatic group test
findings.body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but the route for remove_member is defined as DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). This will raise a RoutingError and cause the spec to fail. It should use `xhr :delete` instead.

findings.title: Remove button appears for automatic groups due to wrong context
findings.body: The template uses `{{#unless automatic}}` to conditionally show the remove link. Inside the itemView, the context is the member (a User), not the group, so `automatic` is undefined and the `#unless` always evaluates true. Therefore the remove icon is shown for members of automatic groups, even though the backend will reject removal with a 422. The group's automatic flag should be passed to the item view or checked from the parent controller.

findings.title: Public group members template may fail if controller does not proxy to model
findings.body: The template now iterates over `members` (`{{#each m in members}}`) instead of `model`. The route's setupController sets `controller.set("model", model)` and calls `model.findMembers()`, which populates `model.members`. If the controller for this route does not proxy properties to the model (e.g., is not an Em.ObjectController), `members` will be undefined and the list will be empty. The controller definition is not included in this diff, so it is unclear if this works. Ensure the controller proxies or explicitly set `members` on the controller.

findings.title: No maximum limit on group members page size
findings.body: The `members` action accepts a `limit` parameter and passes it directly to `.limit(limit)` without enforcing a maximum. A client can request an arbitrarily large limit (e.g., 1000000), causing a large database query and memory consumption. Consider capping the limit to a reasonable value (e.g., 100) to prevent abuse or accidental performance degradation.
